convertedTask.costWarning: Firehose does not have a traditional free tier overlay. You accumulate active charges based on the total GB configuration volume ingested. consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM user, IAM role, or IAM Identity Center permission set.
Do not use the AWS root user for standard learning labs.
For a personal learning account, AdministratorAccess is acceptable while practising.
For least privilege, use the service permissions listed below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity Firehose operations: firehose:CreateDeliveryStream, firehose:DeleteDeliveryStream, firehose:DescribeDeliveryStream, s3:CreateBucket, s3:DeleteBucket

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Open the Amazon Data Firehose console.
Click Create delivery stream.
Source: Direct PUT, Destination: Amazon S3.
Name the stream analytics-lake-ingest.
Under Destination settings, click Create bucket to create a unique target bucket (e.g. saa-analytics-sink-[account-id]).
Select the bucket.
Expand the Buffer hints, compression and encryption accordion section.
Set Buffer interval to 60 seconds and Buffer size to 1 MiB.
Click Create delivery stream.
Firehose does not have a traditional free tier and incurs continuous ingestion fees.
Select analytics-lake-ingest delivery stream and click Delete.
Go to S3 console and delete the created bucket.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.
Navigate to Cognito console and click Create user pool.
Under Cognito User Pool sign-in options, check the box for Email.
Click Next.
Keep the default security settings (Password strength, MFA) to minimize setup complexity.
Click Next through messaging and integration.
Set User pool name to app-student-directory.
Under App client type, select Public client.
Name it web-client-interface.
Click Create user pool.
Open your API Gateway clickstream-ingress-api from Task 2.
Click Authorizers and choose Create authorizer.
Select Cognito as type, link it to your newly created user pool, and click Create.
Delete the Cognito authorizer in API Gateway.
Delete the Cognito user pool app-student-directory.

convertedTask.costWarning: Do not accept default table creation settings. Default configurations map tables as Provisioned Capacity (WCU/RCU units), which persistently draw hourly infrastructure charges even if left completely idle. Switching explicitly to On-demand capacity ensures your database runs at exactly $0 cost when idle.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM user, IAM role, or IAM Identity Center permission set.
Do not use the AWS root user for standard learning labs.
For a personal learning account, AdministratorAccess is acceptable while practising.
For least privilege, use the service permissions listed below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity DynamoDB operations: dynamodb:CreateTable, dynamodb:UpdateTable, dynamodb:PutItem, dynamodb:DeleteItem, dynamodb:DeleteTable, dynamodb:DescribeTable

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) or your preferred standard Region for these labs.
Confirm that your console theme is set to dark or standard preference.

consoleSteps.title: Create DynamoDB table with On-Demand capacity

instructions.text: Open the DynamoDB console and click Create table.
Table name: UserTelemetry, Partition key: PK (String).
Under Table settings, choose Customize settings.
Under Read/write capacity, change capacity mode to On-demand (Pay-per-request) to ensure $0 cost when idle.
Click Create table.
Once table is Active, select it and navigate to the Additional settings tab.
Locate Time to Live (TTL) and click Turn on.
Enter ExpirationTime as the TTL attribute.
Click Turn on TTL.
Go to the Exports and streams tab.
Locate DynamoDB Streams and click Turn on.
Select New image to capture modified states, and click Turn on stream.
Click Delete table at the top right of the telemetry table details page.
Confirm deletion.

cliSteps.title: Create DynamoDB Table with on-demand capacity

commands.text: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name UserTelemetry --attribute-definitions AttributeName=PK,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=PK,KeyType=HASH --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST
